reviews.review:
Risk of Rain Returns is a shining example of how to do a remake the right way.

It takes an already amazing game, in fact, a classic in roguelike games, and improves it, whilst still staying true to the original.

The game's intro animation is stunning, it just feels so epic and gets you hyped for what's to come.

There are many new additions. New items, characters, enemies, bosses, stage variants and the game just looks and plays a million times better.

The new additions all fit so well into the game. The items are all well balanced and fun. The characters, so unique, offering a new playstyle for each one, two of them being incredibly broken and well, the other, well, more balanced. The enemies are all cool, not being overly complicated or out of place, the same can be said for the new boss. Risk of Rain Returns doubles the number of variants of each map, going from 3 to 6 on all the normal maps. They all make for some fun exploration and offer a range of secrets! I love how in order to unlock a stage variant in the logbook, you actually have to explore and find the logbook, some requiring items to reach, whilst others just require a good eye.

As this is Risk of Rain, the core gameplay mechanic is difficulty that is tied to time, increasing the longer you play a run for. It still works just as well and never feels unfair or unbalanced!

The game has a lot of customization, whether it be artifacts that completely change how you play the game to how much % damage you take and deal. There's also options to turn off all the new features that Risk of Rain Returns adds and just play the game as it was in 2013, but with a fresh coat of paint. A very welcome set of features indeed!

I absolutely love the more niche things, like the logbook and the art for all the entries. The lore is definitely a very interesting read, especially the enemies. The character select screen is another thing, the subtle little animation each character does when you select them is simply awesome.

The Providence Trials are a new addition. They are challenges for each character that allow you to unlock new abilities and skins for them, as well as a final trial, that can be unlocked after beating all normal trials. This final trial will push you to the absolute limit, testing you on your pure skill and knowledge of the game. I find it to be a neat final challenge after playing the main game!

Of course, it wouldn't be a Risk of Rain review without mentioning the music. Not a lot has changed from the original and for good reason. The music is simply perfect, not a single track to dislike. Chris Christodoulou is worthy of all the praise.

There's a lot to love about this game. I strongly believe this game should be studied on how to make an effective remake. Absolutely recommend this to everyone, not just for fans of the original, but also new players, maybe those who liked Risk of Rain 2 but were hesitant to try the 2013 version. What I'm saying is, everyone should try this masterpiece!
I like this roguelike. Buy it

Risk of Rain is one of the few roguelikes I've opened up to, and I've been nothing but charmed by this remaster. The visual presentation and the gameplay loop have me mesmerized, and you can bet that it's even more fun when played with friends. Not to mention the customization options presented before you start a run, which just makes it all the more replayable. Give it a couples of goes, you just might like it as much as I did.
